### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2b2e1def086b0ec6f67b96f198282ff2434f0656` — the merge of head `81aa285d588f9eb7e7a42209bb19c34a3d2cdc97` into base `4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2b2e1def086b0ec6f67b96f198282ff2434f0656 && git checkout 2b2e1def086b0ec6f67b96f198282ff2434f0656
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597 81aa285d588f9eb7e7a42209bb19c34a3d2cdc97 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597 && git merge --no-ff 81aa285d588f9eb7e7a42209bb19c34a3d2cdc97

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `81aa285d588f9eb7e7a42209bb19c34a3d2cdc97`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.sys-metadata-audit-organization-column-retired.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.sys-metadata-commit-organization-column-retired.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.sys-metadata-history-organization-column-retired.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.sys-metadata-organization-column-retired.ts + packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.apply-flags.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply-organization-ownership-gate.integration.test.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.cli-organization-ownership-apply-plan-file-required.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/spec-changes.ts, packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts, packages/spec/scripts/build-upgrade-guide.ts, packages/spec/scripts/check-generated.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/migrations.test.ts, .gitignore, content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx, .changeset/23609-legacy-org-read-seam.md

Read: card #23609 (body; claim 6204823952, dispatch 6204866593, os-dev-report 6205946408, seat ruling 6206299338), PR #23778 (body as edited by the seat, 14-file list, net diff against merge base `2906cd8d` of `pr/23778`), and the 48 check-runs on the head (every completed run `success` or `skipped`; the `Check Changeset` re-run after the body edit completed `success` at 02:00:06Z). The head was confirmed unmoved by `git ls-remote` before the read. Judged against ADR-0087 D3 (the entry fields: `reason` the one load-bearing prose field, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` the structured TODO's prose) and its D4 amendment of 2026-10-09 (#22449 B-prime, #22485: both projections leave git and are generated at publish and at docs build), and ADR-0131 D6 (the overlay axis retired), D7 (the `sys_metadata` family carries no organization column) and D10 (the ceremony: read-only plan written to a file the operator keeps; backup the operator's act the apply asks about; apply in fate order with column drops last; a v18 runtime refuses an unmigrated database).

### ① Derived judgments

1. The new prescription sentence in all four entries, "run the v18 ceremony, `os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN` to write its plan for review, then `os migrate organization-ownership --apply --plan-file PLAN`, which promotes or reports the legacy organization rows and then drops the physical column", is TRUE against the CLI on this head. `organization-ownership.ts`: the plan arm writes the plan to `resolve(flags.out ?? organization-ownership-plan-TIMESTAMP.json)` with `flag: 'wx'` (the `out` flag, "Where to write the plan"); `runApply` refuses `--apply` without `--plan-file` first, reason `plan-file-required` ("Refused: --apply executes only a plan you reviewed ..."), before the backup question and the boot. No other flag is required: `--backup-taken` is optional. Without it the run asks at the prompt (`confirm`, which answers false only when stdin is not a TTY or under `--json`) and refuses `backup-unacknowledged` only for a non-interactive run. The pin `organization-ownership.apply-flags.test.ts` fixes exactly this order (plan-file first, backup second). So the prescription as written is accepted at an operator's terminal, which is the reader D10 item 2 names. Right.
2. The new acceptance sentence, "On a legacy database, after `os migrate organization-ownership --apply --plan-file PLAN` the column is gone and the boot no longer reports it orphaned", is TRUE: the apply's column-drops step is the last fate (D10 item 3, the command's own header), and the verified marker it records is what the boot guard and the E1 gate read. Right.
3. Against the existing entry `18.cli-organization-ownership-apply-plan-file-required.ts`: its acceptance criteria say "Every invocation of `os migrate organization-ownership --apply` passes `--plan-file`". The four entries now comply; on `main` they prescribed the bare `--apply` that entry retires. Its own replacement also spells `--backup-taken`; the four entries, the E1 sentence and the mdx omit it. The omission is not a falsity (the prompt answers it), so it is a consistency note, not a defect. Right.
4. Nothing a machine reads moved. Each entry declares `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria` and nothing else (no `conversionIds`, no relevance key); the hunks touch only `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria`, both plain strings. `id` (read by `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` and the registry generator), `surface` (rendered by `build-upgrade-guide.ts` in a code span) and `reason` are byte-identical. `migrations.test.ts` asserts only that `acceptanceCriteria` is non-empty for these entries and pins no sentence of theirs. Right.
5. No generated artifact is owed or left stale, and the dev's reason is right in substance though narrower than the truth. The entries feed three gitignored outputs, not one: `registry.ts` (built by `gen:migration-registry` at install and build; `.gitignore` names it), `spec-changes.json` (`spec-changes.ts` projects `replacement` verbatim; written into the package at publish by the release lane, gitignored) and `content/docs/protocol-upgrade/` (`build-upgrade-guide.ts` renders `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria`; generated at docs build, gitignored). `check-generated.ts` records that `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide` generate in memory and never report stale, so "14/14 up to date" is the expected answer, not evidence of a regeneration. The claim comment's "with their regenerated artifacts" is satisfied by there being nothing to regenerate, per the D4 amendment. The check-runs that carry these gates on the head (`Type Check - source gates`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness`) are `success`. Right.
6. Public surface: the strings ship in `@objectstack/spec/migrations` (`MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR`) and in the published `spec-changes.json` projection, so the change is published prose; no type, schema, export, accept set or error vocabulary moves. On the whole-PR `Clause-②: no` line, the item-6 narrowing of `ServedOverlayRowCandidate` and `StoredRowPlace` is on module-private interfaces in `protocol.ts` (declared without `export`; `index.ts` exports neither), so no public surface narrows there either. Right.
7. The cited files say the same thing as the entries. `apply.ts` E1 now reads "a drop the organization-ownership ceremony owns, and the ceremony has not verified on this database" and goes on to name `--out PLAN` then `--apply --plan-file PLAN`; its `--json` payload (`refused_organization_ownership_unmigrated`, `detail` naming `--apply --plan-file FILE`) is unchanged, and the pin `apply-organization-ownership-gate.integration.test.ts` matches `payload.detail` on the command name, which still holds. `metadata-lifecycle.mdx` names "ADR-0131 C7: `os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN`, then `--apply --plan-file PLAN`". Right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23609-legacy-org-read-seam.md` declares `@objectstack/spec: patch` (with `metadata-protocol`, `metadata` and `cli` at `patch`) and the line `Clause-②: no`; the PR body carries the same line. The spec hunk is published content (judgment 6), so a changeset is owed and `skip-changeset` would be wrong; it retires nothing, widens nothing and narrows nothing, so `patch` is the level, and the body's bullet for `@objectstack/spec` describes the hunk exactly ("No id, category, version or field the migration engine reads changes"). `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head, twice. Clause-②: no, matched.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. `open_questions[0]` (item 2, the seam's raw read inside `publishPackageDrafts`' ambient transaction): answered by the seat's ruling 6206299338, option C, left latent with a dedupe line. The ruling touches none of the four entries' claims: they describe the ceremony's plan, apply and column drop, not the protocol's transaction handling, and every sentence judged above stays true under C. The seat's body edit (`Fixes #23609` plus the ruling line) re-ran the card gates, all `success`. Closed.
2. Dev deviation "spec regeneration" (the claim and dispatch expected regenerated artifacts): nothing checked in derives from the entries (judgment 5). Closed.
3. Dev deviation "derived-gate union run at `042ba4c5`, 13 families re-run at `81aa285d`": the check-runs on the head are the verdict and are all `success`. Closed.
4. Dev's two `out_of_scope_findings` (`DatabaseLoader.queryHistory`'s page cut; `listCommits`' store-order `limit`): ruled into the PR's Acceptance notes by the seat; neither concerns the entries. Closed.
5. Reviewer's own note, not blocking: the bare `--apply` spelling the card retired in the four entries still stands in `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx` and `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx` (mentions of what the ceremony does, not step-by-step prescriptions), in the `sys-metadata*.object.ts` comments in `packages/metadata-core`, and in `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json`. Item 7 named only the four entries and `metadata-lifecycle.mdx`, so these are outside this PR; a wording card is the carrier if the seat wants them aligned. CHANGELOG and changeset history correctly record the pre-`--plan-file` shape and are not edited.
6. Reviewer's own note, not blocking: the sibling entries `18.cli-organization-ownership-apply-plan-file-required.ts` and `18.ups-permission-set-id-column-retired.ts` spell `--apply --backup-taken --plan-file plan.json`; the four entries omit `--backup-taken` as the E1 sentence and the mdx do. Both spellings run (judgment 1).
